item.title: Mettler Toledo Launches eGuide on Preventing Physical Contamination
item.description: The eGuide explores five areas of food safety management: assessing risks, detecting weak points in production, choosing appropriate metal detection or x-ray technology, future-proofing inspection capabilities and leveraging digital data management to enhance compliance.

item.title: Food Safety Caucus Urges FDA to Force Raw Farm Recall in Response to E. Coli Outbreak
item.description: Seven people in three states — including three children under the age of 3 — have reported being sickened by E. coli contamination linked to Raw Farm’s cheese, said FDA. Two have been hospitalized.

item.title: Washington Confirms Bird Flu Detection in Skagit County
item.description: This marks the first detection of highly pathogenic avian influenza in a domestic flock in Skagit County, Wash.

item.title: Smarter Rodent Control Starts Here: QA Virtual Conference Set for April 1
item.description: QA is convening leading pest management professionals, food safety experts and industry peers to share proven practices, emerging innovations and real-world solutions for rodent control in food facilities.

item.title: USDA Promotes Voluntary ‘Product of USA’ Label
item.description: The label is reserved for meat, poultry and egg products from animals that were born, raised, harvested and processed in the United States.

item.title: GRAS Under Scrutiny: Brendan Niemira on FDA Oversight and What Comes Next
item.description: Following U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s recent “60 Minutes” interview on GRAS, QA spoke with IFT Chief Science and Technology Officer Brendan Niemira about how the system works and what changes could come next.

item.title: IFSAC Releases Annual Report for 2023 on Sources of Foodborne Illness
item.description: IFSAC analyzes foodborne illness outbreak data for priority pathogens and specific foods and food categories that are responsible for foodborne illnesses in the United States.

item.title: USDA Shares Food Safety Steps for Spring Holiday Meals
item.description: As consumers across America prepare traditional holiday meals for large gatherings, the USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service shares basic food safety practices that can help reduce the risk of foodborne illness.

item.title: FDA Weighs ‘Snapper’ as Market Name for Certain Rockfish Species
item.description: The agency is seeking input after receiving industry requests to designate certain Sebastes species as “snapper.”

item.title: FSIS Appoints Acting Deputy Administrator for Science and Policy
item.description: Jeremy “Todd” Reed most recently served as chief operating officer of the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service in the Office of the Administrator.

item.title: FDA Urges Recall as Illnesses Rise in Raw Cheese E. Coli Outbreak
item.description: Raw Farm has not responded to the agency’s second recommendation to voluntarily recall its raw cheese, linked to an outbreak that has sickened nine people — more than half of them children under 5 — and hospitalized three.

item.title: Nelson-Jameson Expands Culture Storage and Logistics Capabilities at Pennsylvania Facility
item.description: The expansion is designed to optimize operational servicing, ensure robust inventory levels and streamline deliveries for dairy producers across the Northeast region, said the company.

item.title: Eagle Product Inspection Enhances Dual Energy X-ray Technology
item.description: The enhanced dual energy technology, powered by PXT photon counting capabilities, improves material discrimination by analyzing multiple energy levels simultaneously, according to the manufacturer.

item.title: Caraway Tea Highlights Certification Considerations in Functional Tea Manufacturing
item.description: Caraway Tea Company is raising concerns about how some functional tea products are manufactured, particularly when products include ingredients commonly associated with dietary supplements.

item.title: Richard Carlson, VP of Global Food Safety and Quality at Hormel Foods, Retires
item.description: Jeremiah Johnson, a 20-year company veteran and director of food safety management, will succeed Carlson as vice president of global food safety and quality management.
